segments.text:
> TypeScript → native compiler written in Go. Emits LLVM IR text, compiled with `clang -O2`.
> Targets whatever architecture the host clang defaults to (arm64 on Apple Silicon, x86-64 on Linux, etc.).
> `number` is a JS-faithful IEEE-754 double (`0.1 + 0.2` → `0.30000000000000004`, `1 / 0` → `Infinity`); `int8..int64`/`uint8..uint64`/`float32` are the integer/width escape hatch — see [TYPE-SYSTEM.md](TYPE-SYSTEM.md).
> Multi-file compilation exists (named `import`/`export` plus static CommonJS `require`, V1 scope — see [MODULES.md](MODULES.md)); the entry file's top-level statements still all run in one `main()`, and imported files may only contain declarations.
> No garbage collector by default — every heap allocation is `malloc`'d and (almost) never `free`d in `manual` mode. `-mm=gc` opts into a real one (Boehm). See [MEMORY-MANAGEMENT.md](MEMORY-MANAGEMENT.md).
> Programs are pure libc by default; a program only needs `libcurl` installed on the build machine if it actually calls `fetch` (compiled binaries automatically link `-lcurl` only when used — see [ADR-00020](../adr/ADR-00020.md)).

This file is the scannable index: per-area completion % plus the caveats/blockers that matter most. Each linked page carries the full feature-by-feature table (and, where relevant, its own Known Limitations) for that area — trust the linked page over this summary if they ever drift apart. All detail pages follow one layout — see [Status page format](#status-page-format).
## Contents

- [TypeScript Core Language](#typescript-core-language) — core JavaScript/TypeScript language & standard library (works the same in any JS host)
- [Web Platform APIs](#web-platform-apis) — WHATWG/browser-standard APIs (also implemented by Node.js, but not part of the JS *language* itself)
- [Node.js APIs](#nodejs-apis) — `fs`, `process`, and a real `http.createServer(…).listen()` server — Node-specific runtime globals with no browser equivalent
- [Desktop (`klain:` bespoke)](#desktop-klain-bespoke) — the `klain:webview` desktop-window module, a capability with no Node/Web equivalent
- [Terminal UI (`klain:` bespoke)](#terminal-ui-klain-bespoke) — the `klain:tui` native TUI framework (vendored Yoga flexbox + ANSI diff painter)
- [Cross-Cutting](#cross-cutting) — concerns spanning every feature area (memory management)
- [What Is NOT Implemented](#what-is-not-implemented) — core language gaps, by priority/complexity
- [Fidelity Gaps in Shipped Features](#fidelity-gaps-in-shipped-features) — features marked ✅/100% that still have real, non-cosmetic differences from actual JS/TS behavior
- [Design Documents (TDDs)](#design-documents-tdds)
- [Roadmap](#roadmap)
- [Status page format](#status-page-format) — the shared layout every detail page follows
## TypeScript Core Language

**Strict Coverage** counts a feature only when its row's Caveats cell is empty (zero known caveats/bugs of any severity), over the same denominator as Coverage ([ADR-00205](../adr/ADR-00205.md)). Both figures derive directly from each page's table per the [Status page format](#status-page-format).

rows.caveats:
• A `for` loop's non-declaration init clause (`for (i = 0, j = 10; ...)`) is a clean rejection (the update clause does take comma-separated expressions — [ADR-00156](../adr/ADR-00156.md))
• No ASI restriction on a line break before a postfix `++`/`--`
• `finally` does not run on an early `return`/`break`/`continue` inside an `async`/generator body (it does everywhere else — [ADR-00191](../adr/ADR-00191.md))

• `++`/`--` work on identifier, member, and index targets; the one edge is a postfix update on a side-effecting receiver used as a value, which evaluates the receiver twice ([ADR-00376](../adr/ADR-00376.md))
• `typeof` of a static-method reference outside the covered Promise/Math/JSON tables (`Object.keys`, `console.log`, …) answers from inference, not `"function"` ([ADR-00282](../adr/ADR-00282.md))
• `&&`/`\|\|` yield a bool by default; `-compat=js` makes them value-preserving for same-typed operands ([ADR-00186](../adr/ADR-00186.md)/[ADR-00220](../adr/ADR-00220.md))

Definite-assignment is enforced for a typed `let` read before assignment (`var` is exempt — hoisted and zero/`undefined`-initialized, no TDZ, [ADR-00454](../adr/ADR-00454.md)) — including `if`/`else`, `do/while`, and `switch`-with-`default` control flow — but the analysis is sound-not-complete: a binding assigned only inside a maybe-skipped `for`/`while` body, or in a `try` that may throw first, still escapes (reading its deterministic zero/`undefined` default — [ADR-00215](../adr/ADR-00215.md) — not uninitialized memory); correlated conditions (`if (c) {x=1} if (!c) {x=2}`) are conservatively *rejected*, matching TypeScript. See [TDD-00071](../tdd/TDD-00071.md)/[ADR-00210](../adr/ADR-00210.md)–[ADR-00215](../adr/ADR-00215.md)

• The `arguments` object is synthesized from same-typed parameters (`.length`/indexing/`for…of` — [ADR-00387](../adr/ADR-00387.md)); mixed-type params, a rest/destructured param, and arrow functions are clean rejections — use a `...rest` parameter there; class method bodies get the same synthesis ([ADR-00464](../adr/ADR-00464.md)) (a leading `this` parameter is parsed and erased — [ADR-00373](../adr/ADR-00373.md))
• Function overload signatures are parsed and **erased** — call sites type-check against the implementation's parameter list only ([ADR-00446](../adr/ADR-00446.md))
• Nested function declarations capture enclosing locals (by reference, [TDD-00129](../tdd/TDD-00129.md) Stage 1) but only for use at or after their declaration point, and can't yet be declared one block deeper than the enclosing body — see [TDD-00057](../tdd/TDD-00057.md)
• Tagged template literals have no `.raw` property on the `strings` array (real `String.raw` stays separately out of scope, see [ADR-00028](../adr/ADR-00028.md)) — see [TDD-00059](../tdd/TDD-00059.md)/[ADR-00152](../adr/ADR-00152.md)
• A top-level named function can't reference a sibling top-level binding whose value is a connection handle (`Worker`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource`/channels/`XMLHttpRequest`), a `Promise`, or an inferred-type-argument/nested generic instance (scalars/strings/arrays/`TypedArray`s/objects/`Map`/`Set`/class instances incl. `new Box()`, the value/event handles — `Blob`/`Date`/`URL`/`RegExp`/`Headers`/`Request`/`AbortController`/`Event`/… — and streams + `EventEmitter` — plus `http.createServer` handles ([ADR-00426](../adr/ADR-00426.md)) — are promoted to module globals and work — [ADR-00342](../adr/ADR-00342.md)); a default parameter can't reference an earlier parameter ([ADR-00166](../adr/ADR-00166.md))
• A named function expression whose name shadows a top-level function of the same name is a clean compile error — rename one ([TDD-00060](../tdd/TDD-00060.md)/[ADR-00178](../adr/ADR-00178.md))
• A free `function*` generator may be top-level **or nested** (a nested one captures enclosing state by reference; an array capture is a clean rejection); a generator *expression* works as a top-level `const G = function* ...` binding with the element type inferred from yields, other positions stay clean rejections ([TDD-00096](../tdd/TDD-00096.md)/[ADR-00293](../adr/ADR-00293.md))

• `number` is a JS-faithful IEEE-754 double (`0.1 + 0.2` → `0.30000000000000004`, `10 / 3` → `3.333…`, `1 / 0` → `Infinity`); the `int8..int64`/`uint8..uint64` types are the integer escape hatch (exact past 2^53 — an `int64`/`uint64` literal is parsed straight to a 64-bit integer; a plain `number` past 2^53 rounds exactly as JS does). Bitwise ops and the count/index builtins (`.length`/`indexOf`/`push`/…) also return a `number`, so `(7 & 6) / (7 & 5)` and `arr.length / other.length` are float divides (TDD-00123 Stages 1–3 / [ADR-00377](../adr/ADR-00377.md), [ADR-00379](../adr/ADR-00379.md))
• No `bigint` `.toLocaleString`/`asIntN` ([TDD-00074](../tdd/TDD-00074.md))

• No `.normalize()`
• `.codePointAt()` answers `NaN` where real JS gives `undefined`

• `u`/`y`/`d` flags out of scope for V1
• Several other deliberate scope narrowings (no implicit string→RegExp coercion, etc.) — see [REGEXP.md](REGEXP.md)'s own Caveats
• `new RegExp` doesn't validate its flags string ([ADR-00166](../adr/ADR-00166.md))

• A length-mutating method (`.push`/`.pop`/`.shift`/`.unshift`/`.splice`) inside a callee now grows the caller's array when it is passed as a plain **variable** — full JS reference semantics ([TDD-00127](../tdd/TDD-00127.md)/[ADR-00517](../adr/ADR-00517.md)); residual: an array passed as an **object field**/**array element** (`obj.items`, `grid[i]`) or a HOF-callback element still crosses as a copy
• `.flat(depth?)`/`.flatMap(fn)`: `depth` must be a compile-time constant (or `Infinity`), since this compiler's array element types are static ([TDD-00029](../tdd/TDD-00029.md)/[ADR-00107](../adr/ADR-00107.md))
• `Array.from` iterates arrays, Sets, Maps (entries), strings, and class iterators — generators and `thisArg` are not supported ([ADR-00482](../adr/ADR-00482.md)/[ADR-00491](../adr/ADR-00491.md))
• `.pop()`/`.shift()` on an empty array return the element type's zero value, not `undefined` ([ADR-00157](../adr/ADR-00157.md) convention)

• `Number.prototype.toString(radix?)` renders fractional digits, but a non-power-of-two repeating fraction is capped at 1100 digits and its trailing digits can differ from V8 (base 10 / power-of-two bases are exact)

• `Object.create`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`__proto__` work on **dynamic (`any`-typed) objects only** — statically-typed structs have no prototype link ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md) Stage 3)
• `WeakMap`/`WeakSet`/`WeakRef` are strong-backed under `-mm=manual`; real weak semantics only under `-mm=gc` ([TDD-00112](../tdd/TDD-00112.md))
• Object literal method shorthand (`{ foo() {...} }`) has no `this` binding (no nominal type to give it a shape, no dynamic call-site binding) — a clean compile-time rejection, not silently wrong. See [ADR-00169](../adr/ADR-00169.md)

• A runtime `space` argument and a non-null `replacer` on `JSON.stringify` are clean rejections ([ADR-00222](../adr/ADR-00222.md)) — a literal `space` pretty-prints both statically-typed and dynamic values ([ADR-00639](../adr/ADR-00639.md))
• A statically-typed value boxed into `any` (e.g. a class instance) can't be stringified through the dynamic walker (no runtime shape) — the typed `JSON.stringify` paths cover it directly

• No `console.table()`
• `console.trace` prints no stack
• `console.time()`/`.timeEnd()` are a single global timer slot, not per-label
• A printed string truncates *on display* at an embedded null byte (`printf "%s"`); the stored string is intact — [TDD-00120](../tdd/TDD-00120.md)

• `eval` is an opt-in embedded-engine path ([TDD-00046](../tdd/TDD-00046.md)), not started
• `parseInt` lacks hex auto-detect with an omitted radix
• `NaN`/`Infinity` shadowing needs `-compat=js`, not unconditional

• Type assertions (`as T`/`as const`/`satisfies`) and the `readonly T[]` array/tuple modifier parse and run but are **erased** — they don't re-type the expression or enforce immutability ([ADR-00371](../adr/ADR-00371.md)/[ADR-00373](../adr/ADR-00373.md))
• `typeof` type queries, ambient `declare` declarations, and string index signatures (`{ [k: string]: T }`) are supported ([ADR-00389](../adr/ADR-00389.md)/[ADR-00388](../adr/ADR-00388.md)/[ADR-00390](../adr/ADR-00390.md)); **template literal types** parse but erase to `string` ([ADR-00561](../adr/ADR-00561.md))
• Generics support object/interface/class type arguments ([TDD-00069](../tdd/TDD-00069.md)) and `` constraints ([TDD-00113](../tdd/TDD-00113.md)); a *function*'s type arguments are inference-only (no explicit `identity(5)`), and Map/Set/Promise/closure type arguments are a clean rejection ([TDD-00010](../tdd/TDD-00010.md), [TDD-00037](../tdd/TDD-00037.md))
• Union types (beyond `T \| null`) allow scalar members, object members (one object member, or ≥2 as a discriminated union with a first-position string-literal tag), and a `ReadableStream` member; usable as an **object field** (checked + boxed at construction, [TDD-00119](../tdd/TDD-00119.md)) but not yet as an **array element**; flow narrowing (`typeof`/truthiness/`==null`/`tag===lit`, if-else + early-return) works for a union local or field ([TDD-00043](../tdd/TDD-00043.md)/[TDD-00114](../tdd/TDD-00114.md)/[TDD-00115](../tdd/TDD-00115.md)/[TDD-00116](../tdd/TDD-00116.md))
• Tuple types are fixed-shape structs ([TDD-00066](../tdd/TDD-00066.md)/[ADR-00201](../adr/ADR-00201.md))
• Intersection types are object-members-only, with a field conflict rejected rather than the `-compat=js` `never`-field ([TDD-00078](../tdd/TDD-00078.md)/[ADR-00225](../adr/ADR-00225.md))
• Mapped & utility types are evaluated to concrete object types; `Partial`/`Required`/`Readonly` are structural no-ops, no `as` remapping ([TDD-00079](../tdd/TDD-00079.md)/[ADR-00228](../adr/ADR-00228.md)–[ADR-00230](../adr/ADR-00230.md))
• Conditional types + `infer` evaluate at compile time (monomorphized check type); `infer` is scoped to Array/Promise/bare forms, no function-signature inference ([ADR-00231](../adr/ADR-00231.md))

• **Parameter properties** (`constructor(public x: number)`/`private`/`readonly`) declare + assign their field ([ADR-00447](../adr/ADR-00447.md); `readonly` is not enforced as immutability), and the **`readonly` *field* modifier** parses too — both recorded, not enforced as immutability ([ADR-00480](../adr/ADR-00480.md))
• `class X extends Error` works one level deep ([ADR-00630](../adr/ADR-00630.md)); extending an Error *subclass* is a clean rejection, and `.stack` doesn't exist
• Static field initializers (`static x = 5`) work ([ADR-00375](../adr/ADR-00375.md)); clean rejections: static/async generator methods, a dynamic computed member key (`[Symbol.asyncIterator]`/`[Symbol.iterator]` are accepted, desugared to the iteration methods — [TDD-00089](../tdd/TDD-00089.md)/[ADR-00278](../adr/ADR-00278.md)), and a class expression used as a runtime value
• A field initializer can currently see constructor params (real JS's separate initializer scope forbids this — [ADR-00180](../adr/ADR-00180.md))
• `#x` private names have no early-error check for `#m`/`static #m` name collision or the `#constructor`-is-banned rule ([ADR-00155](../adr/ADR-00155.md))

• The typing tags (`@type`/`@param`/`@returns`/`@typedef`/`@callback`/`@template`/`@satisfies`) type an untyped binding/function/named type, and the class + visibility + documentation tags (`@implements`/`@private`/`@readonly`/`@override`/`@deprecated`/…/`@enum`) are accepted and erased, matching TS's runtime behavior and this compiler's TS-modifier stance ([TDD-00125](../tdd/TDD-00125.md)). Only `@import` (comment-form import) and `@constructor` (function-as-constructor) are unsupported. The `int8..uint64`/`float32` width keywords and `@erased` are this project's own extensions, tracked separately on the page and excluded from the parity figure

• JSDoc type strings are parsed by the real type parser ([TDD-00125](../tdd/TDD-00125.md) Stage 4): union, nullable `?T`, non-null `!T`, `*`, inline object shapes, `Array.<T>`, `function(...)` types, and `import("./m").T` references all resolve. `Object.<K,V>` normalizes to `Record<K,V>` and now works end-to-end (per-key read/write) on top of index-signature support ([ADR-00557](../adr/ADR-00557.md))

• Whole-program compile only
• `klmpm` is Stage 1 only — a `klain_modules//` package must be hand-built, no package-manager tool yet ([TDD-00054](../tdd/TDD-00054.md))
• No namespace re-exports (`export * as ns from`); no npm/`node_modules` interop ([TDD-00053](../tdd/TDD-00053.md)); dynamic `import()` works opt-in via `-dynamic-import=lazy` — real laziness through a `dlopen`'d `.so`/`.dylib` island per target ([ADR-00515](../adr/ADR-00515.md)/[TDD-00056](../tdd/TDD-00056.md)); the eager compile-time-merge backend ([TDD-00055](../tdd/TDD-00055.md)) and a dynamic-or-lazy `require()` stay unbuilt
• Static CommonJS `require('')` works, desugared to an import ([ADR-00369](../adr/ADR-00369.md))
• Node-style built-ins (`fs`/`path`/…) require a default, namespace, named, or `require` import, not ambient; the `node:` prefix resolves too ([TDD-00049](../tdd/TDD-00049.md)/[ADR-00419](../adr/ADR-00419.md))
Completeness map of every TypeScript language feature (implemented / partial / not started / out of scope) — informational, not counted

segments.text: ## Web Platform APIs

WHATWG/W3C-standard APIs — the kind a browser **and** Node.js both implement. Not part of the JS *language* itself, but not Node-specific either. Filtered to those that make sense outside a browser context; pure browser-only APIs (DOM, Canvas, WebGL, CSS, etc.) are out of scope (the **Gamepad API** is being reinterpreted natively over OS controller input — [TDD-00170](../tdd/TDD-00170.md)) — see [NOTIFICATIONS-MISC.md](NOTIFICATIONS-MISC.md).

rows.caveats:
• A timer callback must be a zero-argument `void` function (a closure or a bare top-level-function reference — [ADR-00200](../adr/ADR-00200.md))
• `setImmediate` and a same-tick `setTimeout(fn, 0)` are indistinguishable — `__kml_timer_drain` is one flat fire-time-ordered queue with no check-vs-timers phases
UTF-8 only — see [TDD-00034](../tdd/TDD-00034.md) for non-UTF-8 scope

• `URLSearchParams` keeps only one value per key (known limitation)
• `URLPattern` is object-init only with a literals/`*`/`:name`/`:name?` grammar subset; `.exec()` returns a merged `Map` of named groups, not the spec's `URLPatternResult`

• TypedArray construction is restricted to a variable declaration's initializer (Node `Buffer`'s call-syntax statics are exempt); no `.buffer`
• BigInt64Array/BigUint64Array support an explicit method allow-list — everything else is a compile-time rejection
• Buffer has no `utf16le`, and encodings must be string literals
• No `Atomics.waitAsync`, no `getFloat16`

Complete surface over the selectable `-crypto` backend (OpenSSL/CommonCrypto): digest, HMAC, AES-GCM/CBC, RSA-OAEP/RSA-PSS, ECDSA, PBKDF2/HKDF, key formats raw/pkcs8/spki/jwk; plus the Node `crypto` module's `generateKeyPair(Sync)`/`randomBytes` (PEM, ADR-00434); per-row caveats keep Strict low
`Date` is UTC-only, never local time

• `WebSocket` (server and client, [TDD-00039](../tdd/TDD-00039.md)) has no binary send; both `ws://` and `wss://` work in each direction — the server speaks `wss://` when attached to an `https.createServer` ([TDD-00158](../tdd/TDD-00158.md))
• `XMLHttpRequest` ([TDD-00040](../tdd/TDD-00040.md)) is legacy-synchronous-mode only
• `.text()`/`.json()` truncate at an embedded null byte — use `.arrayBuffer()` for binary bodies ([ADR-00094](../adr/ADR-00094.md))
• `Response.text()`/`.json()`/`.arrayBuffer()` are synchronous, not `Promise`-returning ([ADR-00241](../adr/ADR-00241.md))

• No BYOB readers / byte controllers; `ReadableStream.from()` takes arrays only; `desiredSize` is `0` (not `null`) once errored
• `class X extends Readable/Writable/Duplex/Transform` works (options form too; no `_flush` override); `PassThrough`, `new Duplex(...)`, callback-style `pipeline`/`finished`, and `duplexPair()` shipped (string chunks; `finished` returns no cleanup fn)
• `Blob.stream()` delivers the whole blob as one `Uint8Array` chunk, not incrementally — full per-row lists on the page

• Single-target dispatch — no capture/bubble/propagation (`stopPropagation` is a no-op)
• `removeEventListener` matches by closure identity (the listener must be a named binding); no `class X extends EventTarget`
• `Event`/`CustomEvent` expose only `type`/`defaultPrevented`/`detail`; the fuller WHATWG properties and `new Event` init options are absent/ignored
• `AbortSignal` `timeout` latches only when an await loop checks it and isn't wired into `setTimeout`; a custom `abort(reason)` still throws `AbortError`, and `DOMException` carries no numeric `.code`

• One listener per event, arrow-function-literal handlers only; one message type per direction/channel
• `-mm=manual` leaks per message; `close()` leaks pipe fds
• Shared memory (`SharedArrayBuffer`/`Atomics`) is tracked on [BINARY-DATA-TYPED-ARRAYS.md](BINARY-DATA-TYPED-ARRAYS.md)
Completeness map of every JavaScript standard built-in object (implemented / partial / not started / out of scope) — informational, not counted

segments.text: ## Node.js APIs

Node.js-specific runtime globals — not part of any Web/browser standard, but essential for the CLI-application and microservice use cases this project actually targets. Most (`fs.*`, `path.*`, `os.*`, `querystring.*`, `assert`, `http.createServer`, `cluster.*`, and this project's own `Memory.free`) require a default, namespace, or named import (`import fs from 'fs'` or `import { readFileSync } from 'fs'`) — see [MODULES.md](MODULES.md)'s import-gated-bindings row and [TDD-00049](../tdd/TDD-00049.md)/[ADR-00141](../adr/ADR-00141.md)/[ADR-00142](../adr/ADR-00142.md). `process`/`console` stay ambient, like `Math`/`JSON`, matching real Node/JS.

rows.caveats:
• Async variants (`fs.readFile(path, cb)` + `fs.promises`/`fs/promises`) run blocking I/O under the hood — async-shaped, not thread-pooled ([TDD-00107](../tdd/TDD-00107.md))
• `fs.createReadStream`/`createWriteStream` (Node Readable/Writable) deliver **string** chunks, read eagerly to EOF ([TDD-00108](../tdd/TDD-00108.md))
• `readFileSync`/`readFile` still text-only by design — use `readFileSyncBytes`/binary-aware `writeFileSync` for binary data ([ADR-00094](../adr/ADR-00094.md))

• `process.env` writes work but there's no `delete` (no dynamic-delete operator)
• `process.on(...)` covers `'SIGINT'`/`'SIGTERM'`/`'exit'`/`'uncaughtException'` but not `'unhandledRejection'`; an `'uncaughtException'` handler runs then still exits (can't resume)
• `process.version`/`versions` report the pinned Node baseline + `klain`; real linked-lib versions (`openssl`/`zlib`) and a `--node-compat` floor are follow-ons
• `process.memoryUsage()` reports a real `rss` (peak, via `getrusage`); the V8-heap fields are 0
• `child_process.fork()` shipped as self-fork + string IPC (`NODE_CHANNEL_FD`); forking a different module stays out

• Real Node `http.createServer` alongside the bespoke `http.listen` (now also `klain:http`): chained **and** variable-bound handle forms (`.listen(0)`/`.address().port`/`.close()`/`.on('request')`, untyped handler params contextually typed) — createServer is a V1 `res` subset (writeHead/setHeader/write/end), `.listen` blocks until close — [TDD-00131](../tdd/TDD-00131.md)/[ADR-00391](../adr/ADR-00391.md)/[ADR-00406](../adr/ADR-00406.md)
POSIX-only (this compiler doesn't cross-compile)
• Verified on Linux and Apple Silicon (M4 Pro)

• Multi-argument events via a tuple payload (`emit(e, a, b)` — [ADR-00392](../adr/ADR-00392.md)); no open-ended untyped `...args` beyond a declared tuple
• `instanceof EventEmitter` is a compile-time constant, not a runtime tag

• Synchronous `DatabaseSync`/`StatementSync` over the system `libsqlite3` (linked only when imported) — `exec`/`prepare`/`get`/`all`/`iterate`/`run`/`columns`, `open`/`close`/`isOpen`/`isTransaction`/`location`, scalar `db.function()` UDFs, positional **and** named params, all column types incl. `BLOB`→`Uint8Array` and `bigint` ([ADR-00540](../adr/ADR-00540.md)/[TDD-00151](../tdd/TDD-00151.md))
• Result rows need an explicit shape (`.all()`/`.get()`); untyped `SELECT *` awaits a dynamic-object mode
• `db.aggregate()`, error `.code`, and a lazy iterator are later stages; sessions/changesets, extension loading, and async `backup()` are rejected with a clear message (unavailable in the system libsqlite3 / out of scope)

`querystring`/`assert`/`zlib`/`net`/`util`/`dns`/`dgram`/`cluster`/`tls` done (`tls` = client + server); `https` = client (`get`/`request` over libcurl) + server (`https.createServer`, HTTPS/1.1, [ADR-00505](../adr/ADR-00505.md)); `stream/web` re-exports the WHATWG classes; `diagnostics_channel` pub/sub (string messages); `http2` ships all four stages — `createServer` (h2c) + `createSecureServer` (h2 over TLS, `allowHTTP1` 1.1 fallback), compat + `.on('stream')` APIs, client sessions, constants/settings ([TDD-00139](../tdd/TDD-00139.md)/[TDD-00111](../tdd/TDD-00111.md)); `vm` not started
Completeness map of every Node built-in module (importable / global-only / not started / out of scope) — informational, not counted

segments.text: ## Desktop (`klain:` bespoke)
Capabilities with no Node/Web equivalent, under the [`klain:` namespace](../tdd/TDD-00131.md).

rows.caveats:
• One window per process (V1); a second `new Webview` is a clean rejection; multi-window deferred (engine run-loop/app-delegate rework)
• Raw `w.bind` (string-JSON-in/out, sync + `async Promise`) plus **typed** bind — `bindings: {…}` / `w.bindTyped` auto-decode declared param types + JSON-encode the return, incl. async (`Promise`) + nested-tuple params ([ADR-00441](../adr/ADR-00441.md)/[ADR-00442](../adr/ADR-00442.md)); `--emit-window-dts` writes the page-side `Window` typing; rejection carries a fixed message
• Timers/microtasks/async bind run on the GUI thread via a page-tick pump ([ADR-00439](../adr/ADR-00439.md)); servers/fd-loops still need a Worker
• `new Webview({ serve: './dist' })` / `klain:assets` `embedDir` embed a built SPA into the binary and serve it from an in-binary server — single-file apps, no external `dist/` ([ADR-00443](../adr/ADR-00443.md)); `klainmain -package` wraps it in a `.app`/`.desktop` ([ADR-00440](../adr/ADR-00440.md))
• Verified on macOS (M4); Linux compile-tier only, not yet run

segments.text: ## Terminal UI (`klain:` bespoke)

A native terminal-UI framework with no Node/Web equivalent, under the [`klain:` namespace](../tdd/TDD-00131.md) — flexbox layout ([Yoga](https://github.com/facebook/yoga), vendored) plus a double-buffered ANSI diff painter.

rows.caveats:
• Flexbox is a pragmatic Yoga-style subset (no percentage units / `position:absolute` / `aspectRatio` yet)
• Text is width-aware via a standard `wcwidth` table, but ZWJ grapheme clusters (flag / family / skin-tone emoji sequences) still paint as their separate wide glyphs
• Immediate-mode: the tree is re-laid-out every frame (the cell diff keeps output minimal); a retained node tree is deferred
• The `state → view → update` loop is userland TS over `klain:tty` + `SIGWINCH` — no built-in app-runner / callback-driven loop until the FFI trampoline ([TDD-00150](../tdd/TDD-00150.md) Stage 2)
• Verified on macOS (M4); Linux compile-tier, not yet run

segments.text: ## Cross-Cutting
Concerns that span every feature area rather than living in one of them.

rows.caveats:
• `manual` (default) never frees on its own
• `auto` ships but its escape analysis is deliberately conservative — unprovable values still leak ([TDD-00173](../tdd/TDD-00173.md))

• The whole-program strict-vs-JS axis ([TDD-00075](../tdd/TDD-00075.md)/[ADR-00217](../adr/ADR-00217.md)): `strict` (default) is the compiler's opinionated, safer-than-JS semantics; `-compat=js` opts into JS-faithful behavior. It's a third category for divergences — deliberate design choices, not bugs or permanent narrowings
• Current inhabitant — ambient-global shadowing (absorbs the former `-globals` flag, [TDD-00050](../tdd/TDD-00050.md)/[ADR-00143](../adr/ADR-00143.md)): `strict` rejects a declaration colliding with a built-in name (`Math`/`fetch`/…) as a compile error; `js` allows real-JS/browser shadowing, plain-identifier globals only (`new`-form `Map`/`Date`/`RegExp` stay reserved either way)
• Inhabitant — `bigint`↔float comparison: `strict` rejects it (a likely bug); `-compat=js` does JS's exact real-number comparison (exact even past 2^53)
• Inhabitant — vanilla-JS classes ([TDD-00022](../tdd/TDD-00022.md)/[ADR-00624](../adr/ADR-00624.md)): under `-compat=js` a class with no declared fields collects them from its constructor's `this.x =` assignments, and unannotated parameters — constructors ([ADR-00624](../adr/ADR-00624.md)) and top-level functions ([ADR-00625](../adr/ADR-00625.md)) — take their types from call sites (first-inferrable-site-wins; disagreement on a user function's parameter is a hard error; identifier arguments resolve through top-level bindings). `strict` keeps the explicit-declaration requirement
• Inhabitant — definite-assignment ([TDD-00022](../tdd/TDD-00022.md) sub-problem 5): the TS-only "used before being assigned" early error is suppressed under `-compat=js` (plain JS reads `undefined`; the zero-initialized slot makes the suppressed read deterministic). TDZ and redeclaration stay on in both modes — they are real JS errors
• Inhabitant — real `any` operators + implicit-`any` ([TDD-00076](../tdd/TDD-00076.md)/[ADR-00628](../adr/ADR-00628.md)): `strict` rejects arithmetic on a dynamic value and keeps the unannotated-parameter number default; `js` runtime-dispatches operators on the NaN-boxed word ([TDD-00156](../tdd/TDD-00156.md)) with JS coercion, and an unannotated parameter falls annotation → call-site inference → boxed `any` — `function add(a, b) { return a + b }` runs as real JS

segments.text: ## What Is NOT Implemented
This section is core-*language* gaps only. Not-yet-built library/runtime APIs (Web Platform + Node modules) live in the [Roadmap](#roadmap)'s backlog, not here.
### Medium complexity

| Feature | Notes |
|---|---|
| Spread into a fixed-arity function, a fixed parameter slot, or an uncommon variadic builtin | `f(...arr)` where `f` has no rest parameter, `f(...arr)` where the spread would land on a fixed slot of a rest function, and `Math.hypot(...a)`/`String.fromCharCode(...a)`. The first two need a per-slot unpack against this compiler's static arity; the third needs bespoke per-builtin array handling. A clean compile error today, not a miscompile. ([TDD-00106](../tdd/TDD-00106.md)) |
### High complexity

| Feature | Notes |
|---|---|
| Decorators | **Shipped** ([TDD-00161](../tdd/TDD-00161.md) Stages 1-5, [ADR-00641](../adr/ADR-00641.md)–[ADR-00645](../adr/ADR-00645.md)): experimental dialect (class/property/parameter/method), `-emit-decorator-metadata` design:* reflection metadata, and the standard TC39 dialect (`-decorators=standard`, class + method), and factory `@dec(...)` decorators. What remains: class-decorator *replacement* (a documented static-model divergence) and the standard dialect's construction-time decorators (field/accessor + `addInitializer`) |
| Dynamic `import()` — runtime-variable specifier | Real laziness **shipped** under `-dynamic-import=lazy` (a `.so`/`.dylib` island per literal-specifier target, [ADR-00515](../adr/ADR-00515.md)/[TDD-00056](../tdd/TDD-00056.md)); what remains out of scope is a genuinely *runtime-computed* specifier (`import(expr)`), which whole-program AOT can't resolve — a bounded template-literal form is a possible follow-on, see [TDD-00056](../tdd/TDD-00056.md) |
| Dynamic property add/delete on *statically-typed* objects | **Shipped for dynamic (`any`-typed) objects and, under `-compat=js`, for untyped literals** ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md), all stages): runtime add/delete, prototype chains, descriptors, untyped `JSON.parse`, `Proxy` traps + `Reflect` ([ADR-00630](../adr/ADR-00630.md)). Statically-*annotated* structs stay fixed-shape by design (the two-tier decision) — under `-compat=js` untyped literals are dynamic from the start, which supersedes the once-planned widening analysis. See [OBJECT-COLLECTIONS.md](OBJECT-COLLECTIONS.md). |
## Fidelity Gaps in Shipped Features

Every row below is marked ✅ (or 100%) on its own page — the feature genuinely works for its core, documented cases — but each hides a real, non-cosmetic difference from how actual JavaScript/TypeScript behaves, beyond a one-line documented scope narrowing. Not reflected in the coverage percentages above. None of these are scheduled — pick up opportunistically alongside the open bugs or the backlog below.

| Feature | Gap | Where documented |
|---|---|---|
| `EventEmitter` (100%) | `.emit(event, data)` takes one payload type per instance (multi-argument via a declared tuple payload, [ADR-00392](../adr/ADR-00392.md)), not real Node's open-ended variadic `...args`; `instanceof EventEmitter` is a compile-time constant, never a runtime tag (never a registered class). Overriding `on`/`emit`/`off`/etc. in a subclass now works ([ADR-00631](../adr/ADR-00631.md)) | [EVENT-EMITTER.md](EVENT-EMITTER.md)'s Known Limitations |
| Array methods (100%) | `.sort()`'s custom comparator (a separate C-ABI `qsort()` trampoline, not a direct closure call), `.indexOf()`/`.includes()` (compare a bare register directly, no callback at all), and `Object.groupBy()` (buckets store every element as a raw `i64`, a different scheme than a plain array's backing buffer) still reject a nested-array element — every *other* element-consuming method (`.map`/`.filter`/`.forEach`/`.reduce`/`.find`/`.findIndex`/`.findLast`/`.findLastIndex`/`.some`/`.every`, and now `.join()`/array→string coercion) supports one, see [ADR-00152](../adr/ADR-00152.md) | [ARRAY-METHODS.md](ARRAY-METHODS.md)'s own caveats paragraph |
| RegExp (100%) | `.exec()`/`.match()` turn an unmatched optional capture group into `""` instead of a per-element `null`, and lack `index`/`input`/`groups`; `.matchAll()` is an eager `string[][]`, not a lazy iterator; no implicit string→RegExp coercion anywhere; `.replace()`/`.replaceAll()` template support is `$1`-`$9`/`$&`/`$$` only (no `` $` ``/`$'`) with a fixed-arity `(match, offset, string)` callback (no variadic captured groups); `.split()` doesn't replicate real JS's zero-length-match splitting or splice captured groups into the result | [REGEXP.md](REGEXP.md)'s own caveats paragraph |
| `.codePointAt()` / `.localeCompare()` (✅) | Byte-sequence stand-ins, not real Unicode/locale behavior — `.codePointAt()` is `.charCodeAt()` under another name (no surrogate-pair decoding), `.localeCompare()` is a length-aware byte compare (binary-safe, but still byte-order, not collation). Correct only for ASCII/Latin-1 text | [STRING-METHODS.md](STRING-METHODS.md) |
| `setImmediate` (✅) | Indistinguishable from a same-tick `setTimeout(fn, 0)` — real Node guarantees `setImmediate` fires first when scheduled from an I/O callback (distinct check/timers event-loop phases); this compiler's timer queue is a single flat fire-time-ordered list with no phase concept | [TIMERS.md](TIMERS.md) |
| `XMLHttpRequest` / `WebSocket` (100% as part of Networking) | `XMLHttpRequest` only implements the spec's legacy synchronous mode (no default-async, callback-interleaved mode); `WebSocket` has no binary `.send()`. Both `ws://` and `wss://` work in each direction — the server speaks `wss://` when the klain:ws `WebSocketServer` (or a raw `'upgrade'` handler) is attached to an `https.createServer` ([TDD-00158](../tdd/TDD-00158.md)) | [NETWORKING.md](NETWORKING.md) |
| Optional (`?:`) interface fields, under-assigned class fields, array destructuring past the source's length (all ✅/100%) | Read as a deterministic zero (or, for a nested-array destructured element, an empty array) — a documented simplification, not real JS's `undefined` (no general sentinel for that on a concrete scalar type) | [ADR-00157](../adr/ADR-00157.md) |
## Design Documents (TDDs)

Anything big enough to need a design pass before implementation gets scoped out in a Technical Design Document under `docs/tdd/` first. The individual `docs/tdd/TDD-*.md` files are the source of truth for status; [`docs/tdd/README.md`](../tdd/README.md)'s full index (number, title, status, implementing ADRs) and the backlog below are both generated from them.

Listed below is **every not-yet-done TDD** (Not Started, In Progress, or Partially Implemented). Which rows appear and their Status are derived from the TDD files, so a completed or superseded one drops out automatically; each row's title and notes are this page's own. Several also have a live pointer elsewhere in this file (noted in the row).

BLOB→Uint8Array and bigint, scalar UDFs. Result rows use statically-typed shapes (`.all<T>()`); the dynamic-row (untyped `SELECT *`) mode, `aggregate()`, error `.code`, sessions/extensions/`backup()` remain. Not the KV-for-IndexedDB use [00011](../tdd/TDD-00011.md) set aside

155.title: The native dynamic object model (D1) — property bag, prototype chain, descriptors
155.notes: The design for [00068](../tdd/TDD-00068.md)'s deferred Axis-2 endpoint — the single largest caveat cluster in these pages (~30% of all caveats trace to the static object model). Two-tier: typed objects stay fixed-shape structs; `any`/`JSON.parse`/prototype code gets a per-instance bag (any-box values, proto pointer, descriptors). Staged: core bag → untyped `JSON.parse` → prototype chain → vanilla-JS prototype classes → descriptors → static bridge → `Proxy`/`Reflect`. Stage 1 (the core bag behind `any`: member/bracket get/set, `delete`/`in`/keys/`for...in`, spread, identity) shipped — [ADR-00621](../adr/ADR-00621.md); Stage 2 (untyped `JSON.parse` → dynamic trees, tag-11 dynamic arrays, `JSON.stringify` of dynamic values) shipped — [ADR-00622](../adr/ADR-00622.md); Stage 3 (the prototype chain: `Object.create`/`get`/`setPrototypeOf`, `__proto__`, chain-walking get/`in`, cycle rejection) shipped — [ADR-00623](../adr/ADR-00623.md); Stage 4 (vanilla-JS prototype classes under `-compat=js`: function constructors with boxed `this`, dynamic-ABI prototype methods (tag 12), chain-walking method dispatch, `F.prototype`, `Base.call(this, ...)`, string-concat with dynamic operands) shipped — [ADR-00627](../adr/ADR-00627.md); Stage 5 (property descriptors: `defineProperty`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`getOwnPropertyNames`, literal + defined accessors with receiver `this`, enumerability, real freeze/seal + probes, strict TypeErrors; js-mode untyped literals become dynamic objects) shipped — [ADR-00629](../adr/ADR-00629.md); Stages 6+7 (`class X extends Error`, `Proxy` get/set/has/deleteProperty traps, the `Reflect` surface; the widening analysis superseded by js-mode's bare-literal dynamic default) shipped — [ADR-00630](../adr/ADR-00630.md). **All seven stages implemented.** Remaining follow-up: the slot-storage collapse

161.title: Decorators (`@decorator` on classes, members, parameters)
161.notes: The #1 TypeScript-oracle front-end gap ([00121](../tdd/TDD-00121.md) Track C): 141 single-file false-rejects die on `@`, more than 2× the next feature cluster. Governing tension = decorators can replace a member/class at runtime vs. this compiler's static vtable model (the D1 static-vs-runtime problem again). Staged so each stage runs its accepted subset faithfully and cleanly rejects the rest (never parse-and-ignore). **Stages 1-5 landed** ([ADR-00641](../adr/ADR-00641.md)–[ADR-00645](../adr/ADR-00645.md)): the experimental dialect runs property/parameter/method/class decorators (method replacement re-routes calls through a per-method slot); `-emit-decorator-metadata` emits `design:*` metadata; the standard TC39 dialect (`-decorators=standard`) runs class + method `(value, context)` decorators. Factory `@dec(...)` decorators work across all placements ([ADR-00646](../adr/ADR-00646.md) — the general callee-value call fix). Class-decorator *replacement* is a documented genuine-impossibility divergence under the static model (refused at runtime; future `-compat=js`/first-class-constructor home). The standard dialect also runs instance-field decorators (initializer transforms) + `context.addInitializer` per-instance, and dynamic functions now bind typed parameters and **capture** enclosing locals ([ADR-00647](../adr/ADR-00647.md) — unblocks factory/wrapping/capturing decorators). getter/setter and `accessor` auto-field decorators run — the standard dialect now covers **every member placement** ([ADR-00648](../adr/ADR-00648.md), [ADR-00649](../adr/ADR-00649.md)). Remaining: class-decorator replacement (the `-compat=js`/first-class-constructor follow-up) and static-field decorators; a replacement decorator that reads typed `this.field` hits the general replacement-`this` boundary

162.title: Implicit `any` for untyped bindings + clean rejection of incompatible reassignment
162.notes: Closes the largest invalid-IR sub-family (untyped `var x` reassigned across types stores a scalar raw into a ptr slot). Wiring over the existing D1 dynamic box (an annotated `let x: any` cross-type reassignment already works): route an untyped-uninitialized binding to implicit `any` in the strict lane too (already the case under `-compat=js`), and cleanly reject an incompatible reassignment to an inferred-typed binding instead of emitting a bad store. Operator-on-`any` and compat=js binding-widening are follow-on stages

163.title: `FinalizationRegistry` — mode-dependent finalization + leak diagnostics
163.notes: The `WeakRef` companion, reimagined per memory mode rather than ported: `-mm=gc` gives real Boehm-finalizer semantics; `-mm=manual` gives *deterministic* finalization at the `Memory.free()` point plus an `atexit` survivor-flush (deterministic destructors the GC world can't offer); `-finalizers=report` turns the registry into a labeled **leak detector** for the leak-by-default model (registered-but-never-freed reported at exit by held value). One API, honest per-mode timing (the spec's best-effort clause permits all of it), staying useful under `-mm=auto` too (compiler-inserted frees are the same death signal — they route through the shared `freeSymbol` chokepoint, [TDD-00173](../tdd/TDD-00173.md); unprovable registrations flush at `atexit` since `auto` has no collector). Turns a half-missing competitor feature into a memory-management + debugging tool. Not started — Stage 2 (manual-mode firing) is the highest-value first step

164.title: General C FFI — AOT `node:ffi` (`dlopen` + static signatures + callback trampolines)
164.notes: The split-out concrete design for [00150](../tdd/TDD-00150.md) Stage 2 / the [00032](../tdd/TDD-00032.md) placeholder foundation — the pivot that unlocks opentui's native backend, the GTK/Qt/SDL/imgui GUI crossover, ncurses, and DB clients. Now anchored to Node's real first-party `node:ffi` (v26.1.0, experimental): implement the actual Node API (`dlopen`/`DynamicLibrary`/plain-object signatures/`registerCallback`/raw-memory helpers) rather than a bespoke dialect, so portable FFI code compiles unchanged. The fit is strong — the type-name enum ≈ the JSDoc int-width set, 64-bit↔`bigint` already modelled, `dlopen`/`dlsym` are the `ensure*()` libc-primitive shape, and a *static* signature is easier to lower AOT than Node's runtime-parsed one. Staged A (load + typed calls) → B (raw memory) → C (closure→C-function-pointer trampoline — the one genuinely new codegen piece, the core gap 00032/00150 named). Not started

165.title: Importable specifiers for the Web-global-backed Node modules (`url`/`timers`/`perf_hooks`/`buffer`/`events`)
165.notes: Closes the [Node modules index](../status/NODE-MODULES.md) gap where these worked as globals but their `import … from '<name>'` specifier was rejected. Per official spec the primary same-named export of each **is** the ambient global (no behavioral divergence). **Stages 1–3 shipped** ([ADR-00666](../adr/ADR-00666.md)–[ADR-00668](../adr/ADR-00668.md)) — the import wiring is complete: same-name/`node:`/default and **aliased** imports all resolve (erase-to-global, rename, or rebuild the parse-time constructor node). **Stage 4** is in progress — the **legacy `url`-module function surface is complete** — `parse`/`format`/`fileURLToPath`/`pathToFileURL`/`resolve`/`urlToHttpOptions`/`domainToASCII`/`domainToUnicode` ([ADR-00669](../adr/ADR-00669.md)–[ADR-00672](../adr/ADR-00672.md)), on the hybrid `url` module. Remaining across other modules: `PerformanceObserver`, `timers/promises` — new feature surfaces ranked by leverage

166.title: `PerformanceObserver` (perf_hooks)
166.notes: Observe `mark`/`measure` performance entries. **V1 shipped** ([ADR-00673](../adr/ADR-00673.md)): `new PerformanceObserver(cb)` + `observe({entryTypes})`/`disconnect()`, a global observer registry `performance.mark`/`measure` walk, and `getEntries()` yielding `PerformanceEntry` objects — **synchronous** dispatch. Follow-ups: async batched delivery (the load-bearing fidelity gap), `buffered`/`takeRecords`/single-`type` form, `getEntriesBy*`

167.title: `events` async helpers (`once`/`on`)
167.notes: `events.once` shipped ([ADR-00675](../adr/ADR-00675.md)) — desugars to `new Promise((res) => ee.once(name, (…a) => res([…a])))`, unblocked by the `Promise<T[]>` value fix ([ADR-00674](../adr/ADR-00674.md)). `events.on` (async iterator over a buffered event queue) shipped too ([ADR-00677](../adr/ADR-00677.md)) — eager listener registration, unbounded buffer, consumer parks when the queue drains

169.title: Faithful async rejection values
169.notes: Preserve the original rejected/thrown value (a NaN-boxed `any`) instead of coercing to a stringified Error — fixes `Promise.allSettled` `.reason` fidelity and `throw <non-Error>`; touches the exception + combinator paths

170.title: Gamepad API (native controller input)
170.notes: The W3C `navigator.getGamepads()` shape backed by **SDL2** (`SDL_GameController`) — one cross-platform library gives the standard mapping DB, hotplug, and rumble, so it's a mapping exercise rather than per-OS backends. Reinterprets a formerly out-of-scope browser API, like URL/fetch/EventTarget

171.title: Geolocation API (native reinterpretation)
171.notes: The W3C `navigator.geolocation` shape backed by tiered native sources — V1 is IP-based geolocation over the existing `fetch` stack (zero new dep, matches a headless server), with `enableHighAccuracy` selecting OS services (Linux GeoClue / macOS CoreLocation) and serial-NMEA GPS as opt-in follow-ons; `KML_GEOLOCATION` override for pinning/CI

172.title: File API family (fs-backed data + UI-abstracted picker)
172.notes: `File`/`FileReader` as a thin fs-backed reinterpretation (no UI, near-term), plus `showOpenFilePicker`/`FileSystemFileHandle` behind a pluggable UI-backend seam — `klain:tui` picker widget, `klain:webview` native dialog, explicit-path degradation headless. Ties into the interactive-native-app direction

segments.text: ## Roadmap

Grouped by kind of work rather than a fixed sequence number, since priorities shift and bug fixes get picked up opportunistically rather than in strict order. Core-language feature gaps already have their own complexity breakdown in [What Is NOT Implemented](#what-is-not-implemented) above — not repeated here.
### Next up — bugs found but not yet fixed

Pulled from each page's own Known Limitations sections. A guiding principle: **most caveats in this project are deferred shortcuts ("too much effort right now to do fully"), not permanent design decisions** — where a divergence from real JS/TS behavior is fixable and would move conformance, it should be fixed on sight rather than documented as if intentional, and the ones that genuinely are permanent scope narrowings (e.g. *statically-typed* objects stay fixed-shape — runtime property add/delete needs an `any`-typed value or `-compat=js`, the two-tier model) say so explicitly.
None currently open.
### Web Platform & Node.js APIs backlog

Not-yet-implemented items from the [Web Platform APIs](#web-platform-apis) and [Node.js APIs](#nodejs-apis) sections above, grouped by effort. Within a tier, the same tiebreaker applies — prefer whichever unlocks REST API interaction / file I/O / process interaction.
What remains, tiered by effort:

**Medium effort (new dependency or subsystem):**
- `vm` — lower individual priority, grouped in [NODE-CORE-MODULES.md](NODE-CORE-MODULES.md). Feasibility (assessed 2026-08-23): only a narrow static subset (a compile-time string-literal expression via the existing `eval` fast path) is in reach; anything dynamic needs the unstarted embedded engine ([TDD-00046](../tdd/TDD-00046.md)).
### Later — differentiator features, deliberately deprioritized

**IndexedDB-compatible storage API** (see [TDD-00011](../tdd/TDD-00011.md)) — not started, and deliberately scoped to be picked up only after most of the rest of this roadmap is further along. The idea: expose the real `indexedDB` global/`IDBDatabase`/`IDBObjectStore` API shape (not a bespoke KV API, and not a SQL surface) so hand-written app code using that idiom — and, longer-term, existing npm `IndexedDB` client packages like Dexie.js/localForage, though that specifically also needs `class` support ([TDD-00009](../tdd/TDD-00009.md)) first — has somewhere to run. Four backend directions compared (lowest to highest effort/risk): a hand-rolled RESP client proxying to an external Redis (no new dependency at all — just one missing socket primitive, outbound `connect()`); an embedded SQLite (same C-linking pattern `fetch`/libcurl already uses); a from-scratch native storage engine (zero dependency, matching this project's usual ethos, but real crash-safety engineering); or embedding a mature pure-Go engine (BBolt recommended over BadgerDB/Pebble/BuntDB/go-memdb) via a `cgo`-built static archive linked into the compiled output — gated on a direct prototype confirming the Go runtime's own background threading/signal handling coexists safely with this compiler's fiber scheduler, not yet verified either way.

**Native reinterpretations of a few browser APIs** (see [NOTIFICATIONS-MISC.md](NOTIFICATIONS-MISC.md)) — the same idea as the IndexedDB work above: keep a familiar browser API *shape*, back it with an OS-native implementation. The candidates are the Notifications API (→ macOS Notification Center / Linux `libnotify`), the Storage API's `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` (→ a file-persisted / in-process KV store, a lighter sibling of the IndexedDB idea), and the Clipboard API (→ the OS clipboard). None is scoped in a TDD yet or a committed target — noted so they're on the map rather than dismissed as "browser-only." The rest of that page (Push, Service Worker, Geolocation, Canvas/WebGL) stays genuinely out of scope with no native analogue.

**Mobile targets — Sailfish OS and Android** (see [TDD-00146](../tdd/TDD-00146.md), [TDD-00147](../tdd/TDD-00147.md)) — scoped, not started. Sailfish is the cheap one (glibc/aarch64 Linux: a `--target`/`--sysroot` cross-compile mode, RPM packaging, and its Gecko `sailfish-components-webview` as a `-webview=sailfish` backend under [TDD-00144](../tdd/TDD-00144.md)'s flag); Android is the expensive one (bionic has no ucontext, so the fiber runtime needs a vendored/own context switch, plus vendored curl/pcre2/gc — though its WebView bridge is the best of any platform). Both share the cross-target flag and a remote-runner E2E lane as first steps.
## Status page format
Every detail page linked from this index follows one layout, so the tables stay scannable and this index can deep-link into them:

- **Status is binary** — each feature row is ✅ or ❌, nothing else. An implemented feature with a real behavioral divergence still counts ✅, but that divergence lives in the **Caveats** column, and any non-empty Caveats cell excludes the row from Strict Coverage.
- **Two note columns, both bulleted** — **Caveats** (behavioral divergences from real JS/TS) and **Notes** (implementation/representation detail only, no behavioral gap). Neither ever appears in the Status field, and caveats are not also summarized in a block at the top of the page.
- **One table per category** — when a page hosts more than one of this index's categories (e.g. [TYPE-SYSTEM.md](TYPE-SYSTEM.md)'s *Type primitives* vs *Type system features*), it splits into a `##`-headed table per category. Headings are the **plain category name only** (`## Control flow statements`) — never with numbers in them, keeping the page's own GitHub anchors clean (`#control-flow-statements`) for in-page navigation. A single-category page uses one table and no category heading.
- **Numbers derive from the tables, and appear once** — Coverage = ✅ rows / total rows; Strict = (✅ rows with an empty Caveats cell) / total rows. They live only in the page's top `**Coverage**`/`**Strict Coverage**` line (which lists each category's figure when a page has several), never repeated in a section heading.
- **This index links to the page, not a section anchor** — each category row's Page cell points at the whole page file (`PAGE.md`), never a `#section` fragment, so the link resolves in every Markdown viewer (some IDEs can't navigate a cross-file header anchor and error on the click); it keeps its own one-line Coverage/Strict figure matching the page, which is the source of truth if the two ever drift.

Every detail page linked from this index follows this format.

**These pages are generated.** The source of truth is `docs/status/data/*.json` (one file per detail page plus `_index.json` for this index); `make status` regenerates every page and this index from it, and CI fails if a page is edited directly (each page also opens with a do-not-edit comment banner naming its JSON source). Every Coverage/Strict fraction, percentage, and section total is derived from the row tables at generation time, never typed by hand — an exact integer percent renders bare (`50%`), a non-exact one with a leading tilde (`~93%`).
*Last updated: 2026-08-28*
